text:
maya: ran a quick stress on the 80GB node with two mid-size models sharing the card, hitting OOMs during KV warmup repeatedly. logs attached but TL;DR: OOM ~step 120 consistently.

owen: thanks — which allocator and workspace config?

maya: default slab allocator, workspace cap unset; run command:```./serve --model A:12G --model B:8G --batch=6 --kv-cache=enabled --allocator=slab-v1```

liam: that allocator doesn't reclaim fragmented workspaces well. saw similar on my perf run. suggest trying workspace cap per model and enable buffer reuse.

maya: tried cap 10G per model, still spiky mem during kernel fallback. suspect kernel selection falls back to the generic kernel which allocates extra temp buffers.

anita: can you print the kernel selector trace? selector v2 changed heuristics last week, it might pick fp32 fallback on certain seqlen combos.

maya: pasted snippet:```KERNEL_SELECT TRACE: model=A seq=1024 pref=optimized_fp16 -> ok; model=B seq=256 pref=conv_fp32 -> fallback:generic_fp32 (+1.6GB temp)```

owen: yeah that +1.6GB temp per inference pushes us over. two models + KV prewarm = disaster. quick mitigation: force both models to use the smaller fp16 kernel when available or limit fallback to host-swap-safe kernels.

liam: also turning on KV eviction during warmup helps. we added an eviction policy in allocator PR: `kv_eviction_threshold=0.7` to keep prefix KV footprints smaller and avoid large concurrent allocations.

maya: re-ran with `--kernel-force=fp16 --kv_eviction_threshold=0.7 --workspace-cap=9G` — no OOMs, but p50 latency +12%.

anita: expected tradeoff. can we try buffer reuse: pre-allocate pinned host buffers for swap and reuse them across models? that removes repeated host alloc churn.

maya: test with host-pinned pool enabled (`--host-pool=enabled --host-pool-size=4`) — reduced GC stalls, latency back to +6% but stable.

perf-bot: perf-regression alert: kernel-selector v2 -> mem up +14% / p50 +7% (dev-80GB, multi-model run). linked perf run: https://perf.internal/runs/1854321000

owen: for long-term: proposal: 1) add per-model kernel whitelist to avoid expensive fallbacks 2) slab allocator: compact-on-evict for KV regions 3) host-pool reuse + prewarm swap buffer 4) auto-suggest workspace caps based on seqlen histogram (Optimize).

liam: agree. i'll draft a small RFC for compact-on-evict and an instrumentation patch to make kernel fallback costs visible in the console.

sara: we should also add a canary that runs mixed seqlens to catch these before release.

maya: thanks team — will push a small repro and perf traces to the ticket. :thumbsup:
